A single character has sparsity $1$ and $\mathrm{osss} = 1$: the two agree, but neither
grows, so this witnesses no exponent. No function in the zoo has $\mathrm{osss}$ growing
while $\mathrm{spar}$ stays bounded -- indeed $\mathrm{spar}(f) = O(1)$ forces $f$ to be a
constant-size combination of characters, and $\mathrm{osss}$ is then bounded too.

Upper bounds — holds for every relation

  • \(\overline{\mathrm{prt}}_{\varepsilon}(f) \le \mathrm{prt}_{\varepsilon}(f)\)
    JainKlauck10
    Relaxing the completeness constraint from $\sum_{A \ni x,z} w_{A,z} = 1$ to $\le 1$ enlarges the feasible region, so the minimum can only drop. In the zero-communication reading: the prover is allowed to abort with probability up to $\varepsilon$, and may abort more often on some inputs than on others.

The relaxation is not cosmetic in the setting it was invented for: $\overline{\mathrm{prt}}$ lower-bounds information complexity and $\mathrm{prt}$ is not known to [KLLRX15]. The compression lemma turns a protocol leaking $I$ bits into a zero-communication protocol with non-abort probability $\ge 2^{-O(I)}$, and there is no way to make that probability come out exactly equal on every input. In the query setting, though, nothing seems to be lost -- see the $\mathrm{RC} \to \overline{\mathrm{prt}}$ record.

see also: \(\overline{\mathrm{prt}}_{\varepsilon}(f)\), \(\mathrm{prt}_{\varepsilon}(f)\) data/relations/11-lp-and-lower-bound-methods.yaml

facts: $\overline{\mathrm{prt}} \le \mathrm{prt} \le 2\,\mathrm{R}$: enlarging the feasible region can only lower the optimum.

Why the relaxation was invented: $\overline{\mathrm{prt}}$ lower-bounds information complexity, $\mathrm{prt}$ is not known to [KLLRX15, Thm 1.1]. The proof compresses a protocol leaking $I$ bits into a zero-communication protocol with non-abort probability $2^{-O(I)}$, and one cannot make that probability come out exactly equal on every input -- hence the inequality.

In communication complexity it sits above the smooth rectangle bound, $\mathrm{srec}^z_\varepsilon \le \overline{\mathrm{prt}}_\varepsilon \le \mathrm{prt}_\varepsilon$ [KLLRX15, Lem. 3.3], and therefore also above corruption, $\gamma_2$ and discrepancy.

In the query setting every lower bound the partition bound subsumes survives the relaxation -- see the $\mathrm{bs} \to \overline{\mathrm{prt}}$ record for the argument -- so $\overline{\mathrm{prt}}$ is pinned to $\Theta(\mathrm{R})$ on all the usual functions, exactly like $\mathrm{prt}$.

For total search problems there is an exponential separation between quantum information complexity (communication) and the relaxed partition bound [BenDavidKundu24search]; even the randomized-vs-$\overline{\mathrm{prt}}$ separation was previously unknown for total search problems.
self.name: Relaxed partition bound
self.short: The partition bound with the "fires with probability exactly 1" constraint relaxed to "at most 1"; weaker, but unlike prt it lower-bounds information complexity.
